output:
**What I found:** You'd be adding a `StorageProvider` interface that only S3 will ever implement, for a vendor switch nobody has planned. Don't build it (the record calls this DROP), because the second vendor it prepares for doesn't exist.

**Why it matters:** The interface adds a layer that every storage change has to go through, and it will be shaped around S3 anyway, so it won't make a future switch easier. Skipping it costs little: S3-compatible stores (MinIO, R2, GCS interop) already accept the same API, and a later migration would mostly be about S3-specific behaviour like presigned URLs, multipart uploads and event hooks, which an interface wouldn't hide.

**Do this first:**
1. Keep calling the S3 client directly and close the proposal as DROP, recording the reopen trigger below so it doesn't get proposed again without new evidence.
2. Optional: if S3 calls are scattered across many modules, gather them into one concrete module with no interface. That gives most of the benefit at almost no cost.
3. If the real goal is test doubles, use moto or LocalStack instead of an interface.

**What I did not check:** how many places call the S3 client (`rg -n "S3Client|boto3.client\(.s3|@aws-sdk/client-s3"`), and whether a cost or compliance review is already looking at other vendors (ask the owner).

```
Subject:        StorageProvider interface in front of the S3 client
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: Generality without instantiation (§1a): an interface with one implementation;
                no second vendor is planned, requested, or required. Speculative optionality
                fails §8a, which needs a named, probable next variant.
Outcome evidence: none
Decision:       DROP
Rationale:      The variation the interface would absorb doesn't exist. An interface built
                against one vendor takes on that vendor's shape, so it adds a layer without
                reliably lowering future migration cost. The S3 API is already a de facto
                standard, which further reduces lock-in.
Next action:    Stop. Optionally group S3 calls into one concrete module; use moto/LocalStack
                for test fakes.
Verification:   Not run: no codebase inspection; S3 call-site count unknown.
Minimal alt:    One concrete storage module (no interface), extracted only if call sites are scattered.
Revisit when:   A second store is named (cost, data-residency, compliance, or customer
                requirement), or a non-S3-compatible backend enters a roadmap.
```
